label: verify:transfer-optimizer:reproduce:acquisition() calls a player 'worth buyi
reasoning:
I re-derived this from the code. In src/season.js:326-334, acquisition() treats a package as worth it when bestPackage(include=p).gains.season >= minGain. bestPackage measures `gains` (src/season.js:317) as the sum over pairs of in-out season points against the current roster, so the baseline is "do nothing". The optimiser forces p in and then fills the other k-1 transfers with the team's best unrelated moves. Those moves count toward p's "worth" even when buying p takes value away from the best use of the same transfers.

The result is used without any other check in three places:
- decide(): scripts/notify-transfers.mjs:93-98, the lines '🎯 Тебе: забирай X' / '🤔 можно взять X' for a player a rival let go.
- injuredTargets(): src/season.js:345 and notify :147-156, the line '🔜 X скоро вернётся … 🎯 Тебе: можно брать'.
- 'back': notify :150-153, the line '✅ X вернулся в строй'.

I reproduced it on live data with my own offline rebuild of the notify ctx (same construction as notify-transfers.mjs:19-33). Team 0 has bank 200 and 3 transfers left. The best k=3 season package is +140.0: Randle>Jabari Smith Jr. plus Keldon Johnson>Dyson Daniels. Daniels (1700) is the real gain. He needs a cheap PF as filler to fund him, because his own best single swap is -63.9.

Tobias Harris (PF, 1500) is a worse filler than Jabari (PF, 1600): his single swap is -130.0 against Jabari's -75.3. Even so, injuredTargets returns Harris with soon=true, via a pack worth +85.3 season. The best package without him is +140.0, so his marginal is -54.6. The model's own confidence in that package is 0.56, below DOUBTFUL (0.6). The key 'Tobias Harris:Out:2026-10-23' is in live-notify-state.json 'returns'. That key is pushed only after a successful send, so this message really went out.

How widespread it is: I ran the original and a fixed acquisition side by side over all 8 teams and the top 25 free agents (season outlook), with decide() defaults. Of 125 'worth' verdicts, 91 came through the package path, 106 have a negative marginal (below -1 FP), and only 14 are still worth it after the fix. For team 1, all 25 of 25 free agents are flagged 'worth', so the signal tells the user nothing.

A synthetic case shows the same defect with no live data. Team 0 has one unrelated big upgrade (#96 SF at 45/g) and a mediocre free agent (#94 at 31/g, +1/g). Current code: worth=true via pack 25>94 (+3.9) + 41>96 (+58.2) = +62.1. Fixed: edge 3.9 < 15, so worth=false.

The existing test 'a player too expensive for one swap is bought within a package that funds him' (tests/season.test.js:211-219) has the same flaw built in. In that fixture, the package with #100 gives +54.3, and the best package without him (65>99, 57>98) gives +58.2, so the asserted worth=true is wrong.

Why I put severity at high, not critical:
- The message does list the whole package, and following it is still positive against doing nothing.
- The cost is against the best alternative: 6 to 99 season FP per occurrence for team 0, up to 300+ for other teams.
- The main 'mine' message separately shows a month-sorted best package, which already contains the better filler: Booker>Fox | Randle>Jabari | Keldon>Daniels.
- But the headline names the wrong player and pushes a buy. Following its literal reading (Randle>Harris on its own) costs 130 FP. And it fires for almost every fitting free agent whenever 2-3 transfers are left.

On the finder's proposed fix: the alternative "own pair gain >= minGain" is unsound and should not be used. The pairing at season.js:315 is arbitrary: Jabari's pair is -75 although he is in the optimum, and Daniels' best swap is -64 while his marginal is +103. Only the include-versus-exclude counterfactual is valid.

Side observation: the '🔜 скоро вернётся' message says 'можно брать' whatever the confidence (Harris at 56%). decide() and 'back' do take confidence into account.

label: verify:transfer-optimizer:reproduce:Pre-season transfers (unlimited and free
reasoning:
The mechanism is real, but the claimed size of the loss is overstated, and one sub-claim is false.

Mechanism, confirmed in code and on live data:
- fblTransfers (src/rules.js:59-71) only uses `today` (a date). It drops free pre-season deals from `used`, but still returns left = perWeek - used = 3. It has no idea that before countFrom (2026-10-20T21:30+03:00) moves are unlimited.
- Sports.ru reports transfersLeft = 3 for all 8 teams, never ∞, so transfersUnlimited is never set. Team 0's journal has 8 swaps dated 20.10 and still shows 3 left, so Sports.ru's counter does not bind before the deadline.
- So transfersLeft() (season-ui.js:46-47) and leftOf() (notify-transfers.mjs:31-32) both return 3.
- recommendation() (season-ui.js:432-441) tries only k in [1,2,3], and also applies the rule that each extra move must add 15 FP. The notifier calls bestPackage with k = left = 3.
- The KPI shows "3 из 3" with no word about the free window or its 21:30 MSK end. The branches `left===Infinity?'∞'` (season-ui.js:413) and 'без лимита' (season-ui.js:370) can never run.
- This contradicts the league feed, which says "∞ · предсезонье" (league-feed.mjs:220), and the rules page line "Трансферы до старта сезона на Sports.ru бесплатны и в лимит не входят".

Numbers: I reproduced the finder's season-horizon figures exactly.

Why the claimed impact ("56-152 season FP left out") is wrong:
1. A free deal never raises `used`, so after a team makes the 3 recommended moves, left is still 3. The page refreshes about a minute later and offers the next package. When I repeated the capped k=3 recommendation, it reached the uncapped k=10 optimum in 11 of 12 team/horizon cases:
   - Season: team 2 reaches +207.0, team 4 +646.7, team 5 +600.0, team 6 +730.0.
   - Month: teams 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 reach the optimum.
   - The one exception is team 1 on the month horizon (+142.5 vs +158.5). That gap comes from protectSeason being path-dependent, not from the cap. The repeated path also gives about 154 more season FP there.
   - So FP is lost only if a user stops after the first round, perhaps because "3 из 3" reads as the weekly limit.
2. The owner's own team (team 0) is not affected at all. In both horizons the k=3 package is already the global optimum (season: 2 moves, +140; month: 3 moves, +67.5). The Telegram notifier runs only for FBL_TEAM=0, so no Telegram message is wrong today.
3. The default UI horizon is 'month'. There the first-round gaps are small: +16.0, +5.9, +13.4, +14.8, +21.7 and +4.3 FP for teams 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7. With the 15-FP-per-move rule left in place, only teams 1 and 6 would even switch to a bigger package.
4. The window is the only free window the rules record, and it ends today at 21:30 MSK (about 4.7 h after this check at 13:48 UTC). After that the cap of 3 is correct.

False sub-claim: "If ∞ is ever detected, the notifier prints 'трансферов Infinity/3'". This cannot happen: fblTransfers.left is always at most 3, so Math.min(Infinity, 3) = 3 and the text is "3/3". In that case leftLabel would print '∞ (предсезонье)', so the only effect is an inconsistent label.

Verdict: a real blind spot (wrong limit model and a misleading counter during the free window), but of low practical impact. Low, not high.

label: verify:transfer-optimizer:skeptic:acquisition() calls a player 'worth buyi
reasoning:
The decision maths is right and the claim holds up. The question in front of the owner is "should I spend this week's transfers on a package that buys X?". The other option is the best package of the same <=k transfers without X, not "do nothing". X's marginal value is V*(k | X forced) - V*(k). acquisition() (src/season.js:326-334) never computes that. On the k>1 branch (line 331) it only checks pack.gains.season >= minGain, and those gains are measured against the current roster. bestPackage(include) solves the whole ILP with one extra constraint, `must>=1`. So an upgrade that does not involve X at all (bought with other sales) is counted in X's package and pays for him.

What I checked, trying to refute it:
(1) Is this intended or documented? The code comment says only "the best package of up to k transfers that buys him. Worth it when the season gains at least minGain". No owner rule in docs/ACCEPTANCE.md or data/league-rules.json says that gains from unrelated moves should count toward a player. The only test (tests/season.test.js:211-218) is about a package that pays for an expensive player.
(2) Are the messages honest because the full package is shown? No. The headline in bold names X ("🎯 Тебе: забирай X", "🔜 X скоро вернётся … 🎯 Тебе: можно брать", "✅ X вернулся в строй … забирай"). The package total looks positive only because the other move is good.
(3) Is the gap just noise? No. The dominated packages are also worse over the month and the week (Harris 185 month FP vs Jabari Smith Jr. 205). The gaps are 55 to 432 FP, far beyond a small tolerance. The only small point for the Harris package is that it leaves 100 more in the bank, and the model gives the bank zero value everywhere.
(4) Game theory: in an 8-team league with a deep free-agent pool, keeping a mediocre player away from rivals is worth almost nothing, and nothing in the code models it.
(5) Is the solo branch (line 328) safe? It only fires when X's own swap clears minGain, so it is a different and much weaker issue.

Messages were really sent. In live-notify-state.json, 'returns' holds 202699:Out:2026-10-23 (Harris), 1642271:Day-To-Day:2026-10-21 (Filipowski) and 1641713:Day-To-Day:2026-10-21 (GG Jackson). report() adds a key only after a successful send, and save() writes only when Telegram is configured. Harris is also in 'watch', so a "вернулся в строй" message will follow from the same logic.

Part of the proposed fix is wrong. "Require the pair containing p to clear minGain" is NOT equivalent to the marginal test. Pairs come from greedy matching by position (season.js:305, with a fallback to index 0), so how gain is split between pairs is arbitrary. The truly optimal package itself contains losing "funding" pairs (Randle>Jabari -75, Derrick White>Bridges -56). That rule would also reject an expensive star whose pair happens to land on the funding sale. Only the package-level marginal test is sound. Also, the fix as proposed (tolerance 0) breaks the existing test at tests/season.test.js:211-218: in that fixture, #100 (39 per game) is NOT in the best package (54.32 vs 58.20). The fixture needs #100 made strong enough that he belongs in the optimal package.

Severity: critical. This is wrong transfer advice in bold, already sent to the owner's Telegram, costing 55-212 season FP per message for team 0 on day one. It also affects every rival-release decision whenever 2-3 transfers are left.

label: verify:transfer-optimizer:skeptic:Pre-season transfers (unlimited and free
reasoning:
The mechanism is real, but the finding overstates its impact, one sub-claim is false and the proposed fix is wrong.

What is real:
- The owner's rule (data/league-rules.json fblTransfers.preseason, countFrom 2026-10-20T21:30+03:00) makes transfers unlimited and free until 21:30 MSK. It was 16:52 MSK when I checked.
- Live Sports.ru shows transfersLeft=3 and no transfersUnlimited for all 8 teams, even though team 0 made 8 transfers on 20.10.
- So transfersLeft() at src/season-ui.js:46-47 and leftOf() at scripts/notify-transfers.mjs:31-32 give min(3, fbl.left=3) = 3.
- recommendation() at src/season-ui.js:432-441 tries only k in [1,2,3]. It also charges the 15 FP per extra move rule against moves that cost nothing right now.
- The notifier builds the package with k=left=3, and acquisition() gets k at most 3.
- Nothing on the KPI or in the advice says the moves are free until 21:30. Only the Rules tab says it (season-ui.js:590).
- The '∞' / 'без лимита' branches at season-ui.js:370 and :412 can never run: fblTransfers().left is always a finite number, so the min() with it is at most 3. The ACCEPTANCE.md:188/199 promise of "∞ in pre-season" is never what the advice or the KPI shows.

Why the claimed impact does not hold:
1. The "+56..+152 season FP left out" figures are reproduced exactly, but they are the full gain of the extra moves, not a loss. The moves are not lost, only postponed. Take the free k=3 package now and the 1-2 remaining moves on 21.10 with that week's 3 counted transfers: for teams 2, 4, 5 and 6 you end on exactly the same roster as the k=10 package (season-points difference 0.0). After that full re-optimisation the model finds 0.0 gain for any further k=1 or k=3 package on 21.10, at week, month and season horizons. So the model itself prices the spent week-1 transfers at about 0.
   - The real net cost is three things: the option value of 1-2 spare transfers during 21-25.10, opening-night games (only 2-6 NBA clubs play on 20-21.10), and the risk that a rival grabs a target first. That is single-digit to low tens of FP against roughly 13,000 FP per team per season.
2. The owner's team is not affected. Team 0 is the only team the notifier serves (no FBL_TEAM in the workflows) and the UI default.
   - At season horizon, team 0 gets "hold" with either cap.
   - At the default month horizon, the free-window version (k up to 10, no move cost) would switch team 0 from 1 move (month +45.9, season +37.4) to 3 moves (month +67.5, season +3.6). That costs the owner about 34 season FP.
   - The same change costs team 1 154 season FP (416.5 → 262.0) and team 3 65 season FP (105.1 → 39.8).
   - So "the right advice is the full re-optimisation (k=10)" is false for the month objective. A free re-optimisation has to target season points. The league's objective is total FBL points, so season is the horizon that fits.
3. Through the actual UI recommendation logic, only teams 4, 5 and 6 at season horizon get a different package. The finding's team 2 example (+120.6 → +207.0) never reaches the user: both versions are "hold" because confidence is too low.
4. False sub-claim: "notifier prints 'трансферов Infinity/3'" cannot happen. Even with transfersUnlimited=true, leftOf = min(Infinity, 3) = 3.
5. The proposed fix contradicts documented, tested behaviour. tests/rules.test.js:14 asserts fblTransfers(pre-season).left === 3 (the FBL-week counter), and league-feed.mjs:221 prints t.left as the week's counter. The free window belongs in the advice layer, not in fblTransfers().
6. The window closes today at 21:30. No other free window appears in league-rules.json: countFrom is a single timestamp.

Net: a real but small blind spot that lasts a few hours and does not touch the owner's team. Severity low, not high.

label: verify:transfer-optimizer:skeptic:Transfer verdicts ('💪 Усиление'/'🤡 Осл
reasoning:
The arithmetic in the finding is right, but it measures the wrong thing, and the proposed fix would make the labels wrong.

1) What the verdict is. transferVerdict (src/season.js:312-323) sorts a finished transfer by its expected gain (playerOutlook means) over the month and the season, with a ±15 FP "practically equal" band. ACCEPTANCE.md:111 documents it as based on expected gain ("A season gain decides a verdict first"). Telegram prints the size of the gain right next to the label: notify-transfers.mjs:113/124 uses gains() = "+79 ФО за сезон · +21 за 4 нед. · 💪 Усиление". The league ranks teams by total FBL points, which add up across players. So the expected gain is the right quantity for saying whether a move strengthened a team.

2) Why P(gain>0) is the wrong yardstick. explainSwap's confidence is the chance that the realised gain is positive. Its SD comes from the calibrated season ranges, which are mostly noise nobody can know in advance: injuries and games missed, plus game-to-game variation. LeBron's 80% range runs 612-1809 around 1357. Suppose the means were known exactly (zero model error). A +79 move would still show P(realised>0)=54.4%, and a +285 move only 65.6% (my run below). So this number caps out near 55-65% for any moderate gain, however good the forecast is. It describes outcome risk. It does not measure how likely the label "strengthening in expectation" is to be wrong. "Coin-flip moves get a firm label" mixes up these two kinds of uncertainty. The "even band is hit with 2-3% probability" figure has the same problem: it is the chance of a realised outcome landing inside ±15. The verdict is computed from expected gains, so that chance is irrelevant.

3) The proposed fix does harm. Applying it (up if P_s>=.7, down if P_s<=.3, otherwise even) to the 20 real transfers turns 12 of them into "🤷 Примерно равноценно". That includes Joel Embiid > Kawhi Leonard at +285 FP/season (+3.6 FP/game), Derrick White > Kon Knueppel at +164, Queta > Kessler at +148 and Knueppel > Okongwu at −202. Calling a +285 FP move "roughly equal" is a false statement about expected value. It would hide which rival moves are real threats, which is the very harm the finding claims to prevent.

4) Does the threshold matter in practice? No. Apart from Herro > Okongwu (−11/−7), every real transfer has |season gain| ≥ 65 and |month gain| ≥ 7. Any reasonable materiality band, for example ±50 on the season, gives the same 20 labels.

5) Different questions, not a contradiction. The UI's "не стоит" (<60%) answers "is this worth spending one of 3 weekly transfers on". The verdict answers "did their expected total go up". Both can hold for the same move. If anything is questionable, it is the use of P(realised>0) as the advice gate, which is not an expected-value criterion. Aligning the verdict to that gate would spread the questionable part.

6) Sub-claims:
- Range calibration: ACCEPTANCE itself reports 72% (line 119) and then 73.8% (line 156) coverage of the 80% range, names the tails, and gives the cause (breakouts). Nothing is hidden, so this is not a hallucination. The latest figure implies about 14% too narrow, not 19%, and the miss is mostly the upper tail, so a symmetric ×1.19 scale is crude. Widening by 1.14 moves the swap confidences by 1-3 points (e.g. 70→68, 83→80) and changes no verdict.
- The comment "game noise dominates a one-week horizon" (season.js:367): reproduced. Game noise is a median 0.50 of the variance (p10 0.30, p90 0.71) on the week horizon, so the comment holds for about half of the players. This is a comment-accuracy nit with no effect on numbers.

7) A small real nit not in the finding: the same absolute 15 FP is used for 4 weeks (~1.1 FP/game) and the season (~0.19 FP/game). A fairly even per-game gain can therefore get "📅 Задел на сезон, сейчас не усиление". Example: Paul George > Zach Edey, s +98 (1.22/game), m +12 (0.83/game). Low severity.

Overall: the claim as stated (a high-severity math error, with this fix) does not hold. What remains is low/info: no probability is shown next to the label, and one code comment is inaccurate.

label: verify:projection-ranges-rookies-slots:reproduce:Season 80% range is not exchangeable acr
reasoning:
I reproduced the finding independently, with my own scripts and not the finder's. The core defects are real. Part of the finding's theory is overstated, and its fix (2) makes things worse.

What I confirmed:

(a) Held-out 2025/26 coverage is 0.746: 10.3% of players fall below the range and 15.1% above, using pooled scales low 1.1982 and high 0.7782. This matches projection-report-only.json exactly. The other figures also match:
- The six pool seasons each have an upper-tail q90 between 0.744 and 0.899.
- 2026 needs scales of 1.206 (low) and 1.106 (high).

(b) The UI overstates the coverage.
- src/main.js:207 tells users "в 8 сезонах из 10 результат между ними".
- src/main.js:235 calls the range "10-й и 90-й процентили, проверенные на прошлых сезонах".
- That text arrived in commit d9e7b7c (#81, 20.10.2026), after docs/ACCEPTANCE.md:156 had already recorded 73.8% held-out coverage. The UI therefore hides a measured shortfall.

(c) The calibrated construction is not the deployed one. Ranges.__init__ (projection_model.py:297-316) calibrates on unconditional chains anchored at the model mean. apply() (projection_model.py:578-593) deploys a healthy=True chain anchored at healthy_mean for 369 of the 800 conformal forecasts. I rebuilt the production construction on all seven seasons, using "played the club opener" as the healthy proxy.
- Pool seasons 2020-2025: coverage falls from 0.798 to 0.769, and below-range rises from 10.1% to 13.8%.
- Held-out 2026: coverage falls from 0.746 to 0.702.
- Opener subset in 2026: 0.770 falls to 0.699, as the finder reported.

The mechanism differs slightly from the finder's description. Under the pooled scale, healthy starters had too little below-range mass (6.1%) and non-starters too much (19.1%), and the two cancelled out. The healthy chain moves healthy starters to about 11.4% below. Nothing compensates for the injured group any more. The upper tail barely moves.

The opener proxy is stronger than a clean ESPN injury report, so the real deployed coverage is probably no better than this. The 300 forecasts that average the ESPN and model rates cannot be tested, because there is no archive of ESPN projections.

(d) Miscoverage by player group is systematic, not just a 2026 effect. Across seven seasons of leave-one-season-out:
- Players with a predicted rate under 10 FP per game are covered 73.5% of the time (75.3% in 2020-2025).
- Players at 10 or more are covered 84.7% of the time.
- Under the production construction, players ranked below 160 are covered 74.7% in 2020-2025 and 67.6% in 2026. The top 160 are covered 79.7%, but the floor is too optimistic: 12.6% fall below it and only 7.7% go above the ceiling.

What I refuted:

The "math-error" claim that the pooled quantile is invalid because seasons are not exchangeable is overstated. With seven-season leave-one-season-out, the pooled rule averages 80.3% coverage: 0.794, 0.841, 0.798, 0.795, 0.809, 0.836 and 0.746. That is the marginal guarantee conformal calibration promises. 2026 is a single outlier, extreme (needed upper scale 1.106 against an observed 0.744-0.899), but one season in seven. ACCEPTANCE.md:156 already documents it.

Proposed fix (2), taking the maximum of the per-season scales (block conformal), makes things worse. It over-covers at 86.4% on average, widens the range by 17% (mean width 726 to 850) and worsens the mean Winkler interval score from 1007 to 1043. It should not be adopted.

Fixes that measurably help:
- Fix (1), calibrating the scales on the production construction: seven-season leave-one-season-out coverage rises from 0.764 to 0.797, and the Winkler score improves in all seven seasons (mean 982 to 968).
- Mondrian calibration by rate group: coverage 0.796 and Winkler 1007 to 998, a small gain that equalises coverage across groups.

Severity: medium rather than high.
- Season means and slot values, which drive the draft rankings and transfer EV, are unaffected.
- Draftable top-160 players are near nominal in normal seasons.
- In normal seasons the deployed range covers about 77% instead of 80%. The gap reaches 70-75% in a 2026-like season and for the waiver/fringe pool.
- The shortfall feeds the team simulation through scenarioSeasonScore and transfer confidence through season.js pointsSpread. In pointsSpread its weight shrinks as in-season games come in and game noise dominates short horizons.
- The probability claim shown to users is false for roughly the cheaper 60% of the pool.

Side finding (info, confirmed): projection outputs depend on PYTHONHASHSEED. projection_model.py:58 picks a player's main team with `max(set(s['teams']),key=s['teams'].count)`, so ties are broken by set order. Two otherwise identical runs differed in 648 of 2218 calibration intervals, by up to 99 FP. Coverage moved by at most 0.3 pp.

reasoning:
The labelling in the data is real, but the claimed consequence is either unreachable or too small to matter, so the finding fails the "negligible magnitude / unreachable path" test.

1) Data fact, reproduced. career_games.parquet (nba, season_type='REGULAR') has 6 play-in games per season dated after the last regular-season day: 2022 (108 rows, 107 with minutes), 2023 (112), 2024 (119), 2025 (130), 2026 (126). The game ids and teams match the real play-in fields. The 2020 POR-MEM play-in (2020-08-15) is also labelled REGULAR; 2021 play-in rows are labelled POSTSEASON. The three NBA Cup finals are labelled REGULAR: 401607495 (season 2024, 26 rows), 401734908 (2025, 25 rows), 401809839 (2026, 18 rows). ESPN's gamelog puts these games under its "Regular Season" block, and history_normalization.py:28 keeps that label.

2) Cup final part: unreachable. The only reader of career_games is projection_model.load() (scripts/projection_model.py:500). It keeps only rows with season < min(SEASON_FILES) = 2024, and every Cup-final row has season 2024, 2025 or 2026. For 2024-2026 the model uses the NBA-stats league logs instead. Those use only 002* regular-season game ids, end at 2024-04-14 / 2025-04-13 / 2026-04-12, and give every team at most 82 games, so they hold no play-in or Cup-final games. Grep finds no reconciliation or availability code that reads career_games for 2024+, so "future use would count extra games" is speculative. Sports.ru history does not depend on this file: collect_sports_fantasy_history.py:97 already drops the ФО=0 rows that Sports.ru shows for play-in and All-Star games.

3) Play-in part: reachable but negligible. 234 rows (233 with minutes) from seasons 2020, 2022 and 2023 enter load(). That is 0.171% of the 136,734 career rows used. They give 16 team-seasons 83-84 games and change 261 player-seasons. Mean share change is +0.0001 (about 0.005 games per 82), and mean rate change is -0.011 FP/g. These seasons only reach the 2027 forecast through fitted coefficients, the career-share mean, and lag-4/5 hazard weights of 0.216 and 0.13. - seasonMAE: 249.7223 -> 249.7300
- perGameMAE: 2.5323 -> 2.5325

- coverage80: 0.748 -> 0.738. One standard error with 484 players is 0.018, and two unchanged runs already differ by 0.002 (see 5).

This is negligible.

All-Star and Rising Stars games are labelled REGULAR too, with team codes WEST, EAST, LEB, GIA, STE, DUR, USA, WORLD, CAN, STARS, STRIPES, CHK, KEN, SHQ. 255 of these rows (seasons 2013-2023, all with a W/L result) reach load(). They add a game to stars' seasons and create about 115 false short absences. The cause is that av.spells counts the gap before the All-Star game on a near-empty 'WEST'-type club calendar, using the day-spacing fallback. Example: player 201935, 2015: gaps [..,2,1,..] with the row vs [..,2,3,..] without. The proposed fix (cut-off date plus Cup ids) would not catch these rows. Removing play-in and All-Star rows together:
- fitTransitions: 2888 -> 2881
- seasonMAE: 249.722 -> 249.754
- perGameMAE: 2.5323 -> 2.5321
- coverage80: 0.748 -> 0.725
- rangeScaling (low/high): 1.199/0.781 -> 1.189/0.789
- league short spells per 82: 7.877 -> 7.825

These are still within noise for current forecasts. If anyone does the clean-up, the right filter in load() is: keep career REGULAR rows only when both team and opponent are NBA franchise codes, and the UTC date is on or before the season's last regular day + 1. That one rule removes All-Star, Rising Stars, play-in and Cup-final rows.

5) Side observation: the --report-only run is not deterministic. Two runs of the same code (the provided baseline file and my unfiltered rerun) differ:
- coverage80: 0.74587 vs 0.74793
- belowRange: 0.1033 vs 0.1012

label: verify:hallucination-hunt:skeptic:Season games are ESPN's projection alone
reasoning:
The finding's core claim holds. The behaviour itself was intended, and the impact is smaller than stated.

What is true:
(1) The code takes games from ESPN alone. scripts/projection_model.py:588-589 reads `games=espn['games'] if espn else model_games` under the comment "Games are ESPN's alone (the owner's call)". Commit 22a494a (#61) changed this from `(model_games+espn['games'])/2` and touched only projection_model.py and season.js. No docs were changed and no ACCEPTANCE entry records it.
(2) src/main.js:221 prints each source as perGame × games and then "— итог их среднее". For all 313 ESPN_MODEL_COMBINED players that is false for the games part.
(3) docs/ACCEPTANCE.md is stale in three places:
- Line 121 says "the forecast is the equal-weight mean of ESPN and the model".
- Line 155 says the chain mean equals "regression, or its mean with ESPN".
- Line 161 says ESPN's projected games are "half of the combined mean".
This doc does annotate superseded entries elsewhere (for example "Team result bonus (removed 20.10.2026, see below)"), so leaving these three unmarked is a real omission. It is not acceptable changelog history.
(4) The chain distribution is anchored to the ESPN mean: in 285 of 300 cases the gamesMedian is closer to ESPN's games. So the 80% games range and the season floor and ceiling shown for these players are built around an input the held-out games coverage (79.8%) never tested. That check used the model's mean.
(5) The code comment justifies the switch with "too few games for players who start healthy". The repo's own holdout gives healthyStartBias = mean(pred - actual) = -0.656 over 296 players. Directionally that agrees, but it is small next to ESPN's +8.85 uplift for the healthy-now players. An independent base-rate check also suggests ESPN is optimistic. The top-313 players by previous-season FBL points who played their club's first game averaged 61.5 games (2024-25) and 61.4 games (2025-26) per 82. For the 254 healthy-now combined players, ESPN projects 68.2 and the model 59.3. The overall cohort, including absentees as zero games, averaged 53-57 games; ESPN projects 67.4 for all 313 against the model's 58.5. The cohorts do not match exactly: the median previous-season rank of the combined 313 is 189, and 243 of them are in that top 313.

Where the finding overstates:
- The deployed build is from 20.10, after the 18.10 draft, so "draft values" were not affected for the real draft.
- The UI never prints a number based on "their average". The same card shows the real total ("N ФО за сезон = r за матч × G матчей", where G is ESPN's games) and a "Матчей" cell equal to ESPN's games. The wrong part is the explanation of the method, not the figures.
- src/season-ui.js:328 (sourcesLine), the explainSwap flags in season.js and the forecast.basis field already state correctly that games are ESPN's.
- Using ESPN's games is the owner's documented decision (code comment and commit message). The method concern is therefore an unvalidated choice made on purpose. It is not a hallucination. It stays plausible, not proven, because no archive of ESPN projections exists to backtest ESPN directly.

A related side effect is real: ESPN-covered players are scored on about 15% more games than players without an ESPN projection, who stay on the model's games. Comparisons across the two groups lean towards the ESPN-covered players.

Severity: medium. The explanatory text and docs are false for 313 players, including 77 of the top 80, and the games ranges cite a validation that does not apply to them. No number shown is computed wrong, and the season tab already describes this correctly.

1. The shown rates are mostly the scale factor c, not the player's history.

- The unscaled posterior hs barely varies across players: sd of log(hs/age-group) is 0.025, log(hl/age-group) 0.118, log c 1.061.
- The player's own data weigh very little: median 2.8% for short spells (prior 2400 games) and 9.8% for long (prior 640).
- log c explains 98% of the variance of log(shown/peers) for short spells and 89% for long.

2. The comparison flips with the forecast's origin, not with health.
- ESPN-covered players: median shown/peers 0.47 (short) and 0.46 (long), so they look healthier than peers. 94.6% are shown below peers on long spells, but only 59.7% are below peers by their own logs.
- CAREER_MODEL players: median 1.92 and 2.10, so they look frailer.
- The direction of «лучше/хуже ровесников» disagrees with the player's own logged rate in 228 of 800 cards (short) and 205 of 800 (long). The unscaled posterior and the raw own rate always agree in sign by construction, so this error comes entirely from c.
- Spearman correlation of shown vs own ratio is only 0.58 (short) and 0.67 (long).
- Of 217 players whose own logs are at least 1.5 times their peers' rate (with at least 40 weighted available games), 89 are shown below peers on both rates.

3. Example cards.
- Anthony Davis: shown 5.49/1.70 vs peers 7.27/2.13. His own logs give 8.77/3.16 per 82 available games.

- Joel Embiid: shown 8.13/2.50. His own logs give 20.83/5.55.

His card says «коротких пропусков 174,0 за 82 матча при 6,8 у ровесников», which is 2.1 spell starts per available game. His own logs give 0.63. The chain itself caps the hazard at 0.45 per game, so this number is not even what the model uses. 26 players are shown above 41 short spells per 82 games. Most are two-way or fringe players whose low games forecast reflects roster status, not injuries.

5. The 80% games ranges.
- The claimed 79.8% coverage (gamesCoverage80=0.7975) comes from evaluate() (projection_model.py:437). There the chain is anchored to the regression's games with an unconditional start. ESPN-anchored and healthy-start pmfs have never been tested.
- Mikal Bridges, Julian Champagnie and Bub Carrington have ESPN games of 82, which equals the season length L. That forces c down to the bisection floor exp(-6)=0.0025, so the pmf collapses and the card says «С вероятностью 80% сыграет 82–82». That means P(82 games) of at least 0.9.

- The in-season chain (season.js chainCurve) re-solves the scale against the current play share. It is unaffected by c, so the computed advice does not change. The damage is in the user-facing explanations: 800 cards and every «Почему» block. That is why I rate it high, not critical.
